items.title: Compatibility is more than a data export
items.description:
A data export does not keep you connected. Learn what to test instead. In 2023, Doctorow proposed leaving a platform without losing contact.

That is a goal, not a claim about services today. Export gives you a copy; interoperability connects systems. Before choosing a replacement, test whether the exact messages, files, or workflows you need actually cross over.

items.title: Open access still needs privacy safeguards
items.description:
Does that connected app really need access to everything? Check its permissions and your exit. Doctorow discussed interoperability and privacy in 2023.

When connecting an app, inspect the permissions it requests. Does it need to read everything, or only one folder? Check how to revoke access. Compatibility is useful, but broader access deserves a clear reason.

items.title: Protect your principles before pressure arrives
items.description:
Will your project’s promises survive a difficult decision? Write down who can change them. Doctorow described a stronger commitment device in 2023.

For a project, start by naming what you will protect and who can approve a change. A written policy can guide decisions, but it is not automatically binding. Get qualified advice before making irreversible licensing commitments.

items.title: Possible does not mean permitted
items.description:
A connection can be technically possible without being permitted. Check the authorized route. Here is Doctorow’s 2023 point about general-purpose computers.

Technical possibility is not permission, and not every device gives users practical access. Look for documented formats and authorized integrations. That is a safer starting point than assuming any connection you can build is allowed.
